Particle filter localization

Source: R/localization.R
robot_particle_filter.Rd

A sequential importance resampling filter for the planar pose. robot_particle_filter() draws n particles from a Gaussian around mean. pf_predict() moves each particle with the exact unicycle model under control noise Q. pf_update() weights particles by the Gaussian likelihood of range-bearing measurements (with wrapped bearing residuals) and resamples with low-variance resampling when the effective sample size falls below resample_threshold * n. The estimate uses the circular mean for the heading. Seeds make each step reproducible without changing the global random state.

robot_particle_filter(n, mean, cov, landmarks, Q, R, seed = NULL)

pf_predict(filter, control, dt, seed = NULL)

pf_update(filter, measurements, resample_threshold = 0.5, seed = NULL)

pf_estimate(filter)

Arguments

n

Number of particles.

mean, cov

Initial Gaussian.

landmarks

Landmark matrix with row names as ids.

Q, R

Control and measurement noise covariances.

seed

Optional seed.

filter

A robot_particle_filter.

control

c(v, omega).

dt

Duration.

measurements

Data frame from landmark_measurements().

resample_threshold

Fraction of n below which to resample.

Value

A robot_particle_filter; pf_estimate() returns the weighted mean pose and covariance.

Examples

L <- rbind(a = c(2, 0), b = c(0, 2))
pf <- robot_particle_filter(200, c(0, 0, 0), diag(0.05, 3), L,
                            Q = diag(0.01, 2), R = diag(c(0.01, 0.001)),
                            seed = 1)
pf <- pf_update(pf, landmark_measurements(c(0, 0, 0), L), seed = 2)
pf_estimate(pf)$mean
#>           x           y       theta 
#> -0.02164881  0.02588730 -0.02077261
